Overall an excellent, verifiable, honestly-hedged answer.

Every single ENSDARG ID the candidate reported matched exactly (e.g., slc20a1a=ENSDARG00000020114, slc12a1=ENSDARG00000098096, slc12a3=ENSDARG00000013855, gata3=ENSDARG00000016526). No fabricated identifiers — a strong result for a domain where this rubric explicitly penalizes fabrication.

Against the expected evidence (slc20a1a/slc4a4a→PT; slc12a1/kcnj1a.1→DE; slc12a3→DL; cdh17/gata3→duct), the candidate matches 3 of 4 segments exactly, with correct verified IDs and an accurate, appropriately hedged biological caveat (noting kcnj1a.1 is DE/DL-shared, not DE-exclusive — consistent with the literature). It adds legitimate extra PT-subsegment markers (trpm7, slc13a1), also verified.

The one real gap: for the pronephric duct, the candidate reports only gata3 and omits cdh17 entirely, despite cdh17 being explicitly named in the expected evidence AND already present (tier RAW, LBPP-anchored) in the very verified_identifiers.json store the candidate claims to have consulted in its preflight. This is a genuine, checkable omission that undercuts the completeness of the "project-state preflight" claim. There is also a minor imprecision: the candidate states store records for "these markers" are blanket tier DERIVED, but gata3 (and the omitted cdh17) are actually tier RAW in the store — a small inaccuracy in the evidence_cited framing, though it doesn't affect the correctness of any reported ENSDARG.

Overall: fully verified identifiers (spot-checked and confirmed independently), accurate and well-calibrated biology, honest uncertainty flagging (PMID not re-verified, in-repo atlas doesn't cover slc12a1), but incomplete duct-segment marker coverage relative to the expected evidence. This merits a high but not perfect score.

The candidate answer correctly identifies and verifies 7 of 8 expected markers with proper ENSDARG IDs and demonstrates exemplary verification practice (live re-verification, raw response caching per CLAUDE.md §7.9).
